title: Relative Proj on an algebraic space: scheme tests and arbitrary base change
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal A_n$ be a commutative unital graded $\mathcal O_X$-algebra on the small etale site [def-trf-etale-graded-module-algebra], with each $\mathcal A_n$ quasi-coherent [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Pullbacks mean tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. There is an algebraic space $P_X(\mathcal A)$ with a morphism $p:P_X(\mathcal A)\to X$ representable by schemes. For every $S$-scheme $W$ and morphism $g:W\to X$, there is a canonical isomorphism of $W$-schemes
$$W\times_XP_X(\mathcal A)\simeq\operatorname{Proj}_W((g^*\mathcal A)_{\mathrm{Zar}}),$$
where degreewise passage to the Zariski site uses [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] and the scheme relative Proj is [def-nagata-relative-proj]. These comparisons commute with further scheme base change and the projections to $W$; they determine $P_X(\mathcal A)$ up to unique isomorphism preserving the comparisons. For every morphism $h:Y\to X$ of algebraic spaces over $S$, there is a canonical isomorphism
$$P_Y(h^*\mathcal A)\simeq Y\times_XP_X(\mathcal A),$$
compatible with the scheme-test comparisons, identity base change and composition. A graded $\mathcal O_X$-algebra isomorphism $e:\mathcal A\simeq\mathcal B$ induces a canonical isomorphism $P_X(\mathcal B)\simeq P_X(\mathcal A)$, compatible with these base-change identifications; on a scheme test it is the ordinary relative-Proj isomorphism induced by $e$. No finite generation, flatness, Noetherian, separation or quasi-compactness assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Tensor pullback preserves quasi-coherence degreewise by [lem-sfb-space-module-pullback-quasicoherent]. The tensor isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] pulls back the homogeneous products and unit, giving the graded algebras in the statement. On a scheme the Zariski/etale equivalence [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] identifies these operations: locally both are scalar extension, with product $(b\otimes x)(c\otimes y)=bc\otimes xy$ and unit $1\otimes1$. Use the normalized compositors of [def-sfb-space-module-tensor-composition] throughout. On iterated local tensors the two three-map composites both send $b\otimes(c\otimes(d\otimes x))$ to $bc'd'\otimes x$, where primes denote restriction to the final chart; the unit sends $1\otimes x$ to $x$. Thus these comparisons respect products, units, identities and composition. These are comparisons of sheaves and homogeneous maps, not assertions that sections commute with infinite direct sums.

source.place: Tag 084B (lemma-relative-proj), scheme coefficient identification; 085C (lemma-relative-proj-base-change), identification of successive pullbacks.

proof.text: For a quasi-compact $S$-scheme $T$ define $F_{X,\mathcal A}(T)$ using quadruples $(d,f:T\to X,\mathcal L,\psi)$: $d\geq1$, $\mathcal L$ is an ordinary invertible module on $T$, and $\psi:(f^*\mathcal A)_{\rm Zar}^{(d)}\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$ is a graded unital map surjective in degree one. Here $(\mathcal A^{(d)})_n=\mathcal A_{dn}$. Identify two quadruples with the same $f$ when, for some $m=ad=a'd'>0$, there is $\beta:\mathcal L^{\otimes a}\simeq(\mathcal L')^{\otimes a'}$ satisfying $\beta^{\otimes n}\psi_{an}=\psi'_{a'n}$ for every $n$. This is an equivalence relation: the identity and inverse witnesses give reflexivity and symmetry; for transitivity raise two witnesses to a common multiple of their degrees, then compose the resulting isomorphisms and their tensor powers. Invertible tensor powers and their pullbacks are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor]. This is the quotient relation of [lem-sfb-scheme-proj-veronese-quotient-functor] on scheme bases; the same explicit relation makes sense for the present $f$. The projection to $X(T)$ remembers $f$.

source.place: Paragraphs before Tag 084B (lemma-relative-proj): quadruples, common-multiple equivalence and equation-proj.

proof.text: For arbitrary $T$ set $F(T)=\varprojlim_{V\subseteq T\ {\rm qc\ open}}F(V)$. On a quasi-compact $T$ this recovers the preceding definition because $T$ is itself an index. To pull a family back along $u:T'\to T$, take a quasi-compact open $V'\subseteq T'$ and choose a quasi-compact open $V\subseteq T$ containing $u(V')$; finitely many affine opens covering the quasi-compact image give such $V$. Pull the representative over $V$ back to $V'$. Its line remains invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor]. Pullback preserves the surjection: it is a cokernel, and module pullback of Zariski modules on schemes is a left adjoint [def-pc-module-pullback], so preserves cokernels by [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]. Step 1 identifies its source and tensor powers. Equivalent data remain equivalent by pulling back their witnesses. Different choices of $V$ agree by comparison with their quasi-compact union. The same argument for inclusions of $V'$ gives a compatible family; the identity and composite formulas of step 1 prove the functor laws. The remembered maps $V\to X$ agree on every quasi-compact open of each intersection, hence on the intersection, and glue uniquely to $T\to X$, since $X$ is a sheaf [def-trf-algebraic-space]. This defines a presheaf $F$ and a natural transformation $F\to X$. No intersection is assumed quasi-compact or affine.

source.place: Paragraphs before Tag 084B (lemma-relative-proj): extension to arbitrary schemes and functoriality of equation-proj.

proof.text: Fix $g:W\to X$ with $W$ a scheme, and set $\mathcal B=(g^*\mathcal A)_{\rm Zar}$. On quasi-compact $T$, a section of $h_W\times_X F$ is a map $a:T\to W$ and a quadruple $(d,f,\mathcal L,\psi)$ with $f=g\circ a$. The compositor and scheme comparison of step 1 identify its source with $a^*\mathcal B^{(d)}$. Send it to $(d,a,\mathcal L,\psi)$ in $Q_{W,\mathcal B}(T)$. The inverse replaces $a$ by $g\circ a$ and retains the same line and homogeneous maps. They are inverse on equivalence classes because the witnesses are literally unchanged. For arbitrary $T$, perform this on quasi-compact opens; the maps to $W$ glue uniquely and both constructions commute with restriction. Therefore $h_W\times_XF\simeq Q_{W,\mathcal B}$. By [lem-sfb-scheme-proj-veronese-quotient-functor] the latter is represented by $\operatorname{Proj}_W(\mathcal B)$. The structural map remembers $a$. Replacing $W$ by a scheme $W'\to W$ simply replaces $a$ by its factorization through $W'$ and leaves $d,\mathcal L,\psi$ unchanged. This proves the claimed naturality under further scheme base change, including the projections.

source.place: Tag 084B (lemma-relative-proj), proof: explicit identification of the scheme quadruple functor with the fibre product.

proof.text: Each scheme in step 4 is an algebraic space by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. Apply [lem-sfb-presheaf-space-target-bootstrap] to $F\to X$: it requires a presheaf and the algebraicity of all scheme-test fibre products, both established above; no sheaf hypothesis on $F$ is needed. Thus $P_X(\mathcal A):=F$ is an algebraic space. Its map to $X$ is representable by schemes by step 4 and the definition [def-trf-algebraic-space]; the presheaf fibre products are now the sheaf fibre products. These give exactly the comparisons of the statement. For uniqueness, let another algebraic space $P$ over $X$ carry the same natural comparisons. For $q\in P(T)$ with image $g:T\to X$, apply its $W=T$ comparison to $(\operatorname{id}_T,q)$ and then the inverse of our comparison. This gives an element of $F(T)$ with image $g$. The reverse construction gives inverse maps, natural in $T$ by the compatibility of the comparisons. They therefore define inverse algebraic-space morphisms. Any morphism preserving the comparisons must act by this formula on every $q$, which proves uniqueness.

Let $h:Y\to X$ be arbitrary. Step 1 ensures that $h^*\mathcal A$ is a graded quasi-coherent algebra, so the construction applies on $Y$. On a quasi-compact test $T$ define
$$[d,b:T\to Y,\mathcal L,\psi]\longmapsto\bigl(b,[d,h\circ b,\mathcal L,\psi]\bigr).$$
The sources of $\psi$ agree by the normalized pullback compositor. Conversely a pair $(b,[d,f,\mathcal L,\psi])$ in the fibre product satisfies $f=h\circ b$; replace $f$ by $b$ to obtain its preimage. Both operations leave every equivalence witness unchanged, are inverse and commute with scheme restriction. They extend to arbitrary tests by the compatible families of step 3, yielding an isomorphism $F_{Y,h^*\mathcal A}\simeq Y\times_XF_{X,\mathcal A}$; the right side is an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. For an identity $h$ the formula retains the original quadruple. For $Z\xrightarrow{k}Y\xrightarrow{h}X$, both successive and direct comparisons send $[d,c,\mathcal L,\psi]$ to $(c,[d,hkc,\mathcal L,\psi])$, under the projection-preserving fibre-product associator. Step 1 identifies the sources of $\psi$ coherently. The formula is also the one in step 4 on every scheme test, proving all base-change compatibilities without flatness.

source.place: Tag 085C (lemma-relative-proj-base-change), proof and inverse on quadruples.

proof.text: For a graded isomorphism $e:\mathcal A\simeq\mathcal B$, send a $\mathcal B$-quadruple to the $\mathcal A$-quadruple with the same $d,f,\mathcal L$ and map $\psi\circ(f^*e)^{(d)}$. Degree-one surjectivity remains true because $f^*e_d$ is invertible. Precomposition retains each common-power equivalence witness; the inverse uses $e^{-1}$. The maps commute with restriction and thus define inverse morphisms $P_X(\mathcal B)\simeq P_X(\mathcal A)$. Under any base change the two possible composites have homogeneous maps $\psi_{n}\circ f^*e_{dn}$ after the compositor, so coincide. On a scheme test this is the ordinary relative-Proj isomorphism by the normalization in [lem-sfb-scheme-proj-veronese-quotient-functor]. The arguments used neither finite generation nor any flatness, separation, quasi-compactness or Noetherian hypothesis on the base spaces.
